resolutions.researcher_notes: MEED names 'the Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line (HDUG-1)' as an existing, in-service trunk that the new Hawiyah NGL plant is being tied into via a 48-inch/25-km inlet-outlet line (tender 2005, mechanical completion 2007). An existing gas line being connected to downstream plant expansions implies operating status by context (status is inferred, not literal). Single strong trade source (seed OPEC ASB cites are generic Saudi gas-grid pages, not pipeline-specific and route to gem.wiki).
MEED explicitly calls it the 'Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line (HDUG-1)' — commodity = gas confirmed by name and by its role in the Hawiyah gas/NGL processing programme. Single trade source.

No independent source found stating the 87 mi / 140 km length for HDUG-1. MEED, offshore-technology, DMS Projects, Wikipedia (Haradh gas plant) and Aramco publications give no length for the Haradh-Uthmaniyah line itself; the 87 mi/140 km figure appears to be a GEM estimate. UNRESOLVED — length value unsupported by any verifiable outside source.

VALUE FLAG: the only '48-inch' figure found refers to the 25-km inlet/outlet line between the Hawiyah NGL plant and HDUG-1 — NOT to HDUG-1's own diameter ('a 48-inch, 25-kilometre inlet and outlet line between the new Hawiyah NGL plant and the Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line (HDUG-1)'). No source states the Haradh-Uthmaniya trunk itself is 48 in; GEM's 48-in value looks like a misread of that connecting-line spec. UNRESOLVED pending a source that gives HDUG-1's own diameter.

MEED names the 'Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line (HDUG-1)' — the line originates at the Haradh gas plant (FuelSource=Haradh consistent with the naming and the Haradh gas-processing program). Single trade source.

MEED confirms the Haradh->Uthmaniyah endpoints (HDUG-1, Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line). Wikipedia (Haradh gas plant) independently places the Haradh gas plant in the Eastern Province; Haradh sits in the Al-Ahsa (Ahsa) governorate, and Uthmaniyah is also in the Eastern Province, matching Start=Ahsa/Eastern Province, End=Uthmaniya/Eastern Province. Two independent sources on endpoints/province.

HDUG-1 is part of Saudi Aramco's Hawiyah/Haradh gas-processing infrastructure (MEED); Aramco 100% owner consistent with all Saudi domestic gas-grid trunks. Single trade source (Aramco ownership is uncontested for Saudi domestic gas pipelines).
